subject: Performance SLOs & VPC qualification - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLOs & VPC qualification - next steps

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can get your Private/VPC perf qualification scheduled: 

Summary from call:
- Target latency: P95 generation latency <= 150ms for streaming responses at 512-token average (we heard this is your SLO).
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline 200 req/s sustained, peak bursts to 500 req/s; expected concurrency ~50 workers.
- Streaming requirements: chunked streaming with server-side flush every ~200ms; client expects low tail latency.
- Model footprint: roughly 70B quantized model with warmed KV-cache on hot paths.
- Internal latency budget: you mentioned 60ms for internal app routing + network edges.

Network/VPC topics to validate:
- Do you have route for direct peering (AWS Transit Gateway / VPC Peering) or will you require IPSec VPN? (peering preferred for stable latency)
- Egress path & IPs: where will traffic to Redwood Dedicated sit (public egress, NAT, NGW)?
- Firewall/IDS: any rules that could reassemble/inspect streaming chunks or terminate long-lived TLS sessions?
- Expected QPS from each AZ/region and whether you plan to distribute across multiple VPCs.

Action items we need from Acme to scope the test and book a validation window:
1) Network diagram showing VPCs, NAT/IGW, Transit Gateway, firewall appliances, and egress path (attach traceroute if available).
2) Current egress bandwidth and per-connection packet loss statistics (1-hr sample).
3) Confirmation whether peering is feasible; if not, details on VPN concentrator, throughput, and PSK/Certificates policy.
4) Preferred test windows (we recommend a 2-hr low-traffic window + a 1-hr peak-stress window).

Attachments: post-call-matters.pdf (recap + checklist), redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf (what we'll run during the validation).

Next step: Can you share the network diagram and confirm whether peering is possible? If yes, we can provision a test CIDR and schedule the test on your preferred window (we have openings Tues 8/18 & Wed 8/19).

Thanks — looping Jordan & Rishi for technical validation and to own the test-run coordination.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>

Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & VPC qualification - next steps

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. Attached a high-level network diagram and our current egress policy. A few answers inline: 

- Peering: We can open an AWS Transit Gateway attachment to Redwood (preferred). We will need a short security review but expect to be able to approve by EOD Monday.
- VPN: If peering isn’t approved, we have an IPSec concentrator (through our managed FW vendor). Throughput is limited to ~1.2 Gbps on a single tunnel; we can do multiple tunnels but routing will add ~5–10ms overhead.
- Egress path: Traffic will egress through NAT Gateway in our primary VPC in us-west-2, then go through our outbound proxy cluster. IPs and CIDR in egress-policy.txt.
- Firewall/IDS: We do have an inline IDS that performs TLS metadata inspection but not full TLS termination. It can interrupt long-lived connections if it sees anomalous patterns; we'll whitelist the test CIDRs.

Network attachments included:
- acme-network-diagram.png
- egress-policy.txt

We can provision peering and open the firewall rules for a test window on Tue 2026-08-18 between 03:00–06:00 UTC (low-traffic) and 17:00–19:00 UTC (possible burst window).

Let me know what specific traceroutes or packet captures you want; we can provide a 1-hour pcap and a 5-minute continuous traceroute from our egress NAT IPs.

Thanks,
Alice Johnson
Sr. SRE, Acme Corp
alice.johnson@acme.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 07:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & VPC qualification - next steps

Alice —

Great, thanks for the quick response and the artifacts. A few technical clarifications and the test plan we will run: 

Clarifications: 
- TLS termination: where does TLS terminate today? If your outbound proxy does TLS re-encryption we need to understand per-connection keepalive semantics. Long-lived streaming connections should not be re-negotiated every ~60s.
- P95 budgeting: assume network transit (egress NAT -> Redwood peering edge) will add ~15–30ms typical; we account for host+runtime overhead ~40–80ms depending on model and KV-cache hit. That leaves ~40–60ms headroom for application and any additional middleboxes to meet your 150ms P95.

Proposed validation steps (we'll run these from Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2):
1) Baseline latency test: 1k lightweight requests (no payload) to validate RTT & TLS handshakes.
2) Streaming perf: sustained streaming at your target concurrency (50) with average 512-token responses; measure P50/P95/P99 and chunk flush intervals.
3) Throughput soak: ramp to 200 req/s sustained for 30 minutes, then burst to 500 req/s for 5 minutes to validate autoscaling/queue behavior.
4) Packet-level verification: run traceroutes and request your 1-hr pcap to correlate packet loss with observed tail latency.

We have a public runbook with the test script and sample configs: https://drive.redwood.com/perf/runbooks/vpc-test-plan (attached vpc-test-plan.md).

Ask for Acme prep:
- If peering is possible, please confirm the peering CIDR and provide the eBGP/route acceptance policy or allow us to advertise a /28 for the tests.
- If using VPN, confirm number of parallel tunnels and expected per-tunnel throughput.
- Provide a 1-hour pcap and the traceroute sequence 30m before the test window.

We can run the baseline + streaming perf on Tue 2026-08-18 03:00–05:00 UTC and the throughput soak during the 17:00–18:00 UTC window if that works for your team. If peering isn't green-lit by EOD Monday we'll pivot to VPN but will need the pre-shared key and tunnel endpoints from your VPN admin.

Jordan Blake
